newsitem.title: USA: Labelling U.S. gene-altered beans unnecessary - Moos.
newsitem.headline: Labelling U.S. gene-altered beans unnecessary - Moos.

text.p: Labelling U.S. gene-altered soybeans going into the European Union is unnecessary, and would be impossible, said Agriculture Under Secretary Gene Moos on Thursday.
"There's no need for labelling," Moos told Reuters. "We see no reason why labelling should be required, and we think it would be impossible on top of that."

Moos said that USDA officials are keeping a close eye on statements from a European retail group about a possible boycott of soy products, but said the U.S. government would probably not be able to interfere with a private boycott.

"I don't know what we could do about this, other than appeal to the EU govenment that they try to get their private industry to honor the agreement ... but this is not a result of any government imposed access ... it's a matter for the private sector to sort out," Moos said.

Moos said that the EU government has approved the safety of the genetically altered soybeans developed by St. Louis-based Monsanto Co which were planted by U.S. farmers on a commercial basis for the first time this past season.

EuroCommerce, a group which represents the retail and wholesale sector in 20 European countries, said Thursday in Brussels that U.S. farmers could risk losing their European soybean markets if consumers decide to boycott soy products unless the products from gene-altered soybeans are labelled.
EuroCommerce said it was not against genetic engineering of food, but that it wanted the products to be labelled to address any consumer concerns.

Moos said that U.S. officials in Brussels have been asked to keep Washington officials informed of the situation, but at this point there have been no formal discussions between U.S. and EU officials.
Asked how serious this latest development might be, Moos said, "This is always a threat, but how serious it is is unclear at this point."
